FDA Accepts Krystal Biotech's Biologics License Application for Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa

PITTSBURGH, June 2022 -- Krystal Biotech, Inc. (NASDAQ: KRYS), a biotechnology company
developing and commercializing genetic medicines to treat diseases with high unmet medical
needs, today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has accepted for
filing the company's Biologics License Application (BLA) for beremagene geperpavec (B-VEC,
formerly KB103) for the treatment of dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa (DEB).

The FDA has granted Priority Review to the BLA and has set a Prescription Drug User Fee Act
(PDUFA) target action date of February 17, 2023.

"The acceptance of our BLA and the granting of Priority Review are important milestones for
patients living with DEB, a devastating and often fatal genetic skin disease for which there
are no approved therapies," said Krish S. Krishnan, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of
Krystal Biotech.

B-VEC is a redosable, topical gene therapy designed to deliver two copies of the COL7A1 gene
directly to a patient's skin cells. The BLA is supported by data from the pivotal Phase 3
GEM-3 study, in which the trial met both its primary endpoint of complete wound healing at
six months and its key secondary endpoint of complete wound healing at three months, each
with high statistical significance (p<0.001).

B-VEC has received Breakthrough Therapy, Fast Track, Rare Pediatric Disease and Orphan Drug
designations from the FDA. The company noted there is no prior Complete Response Letter for
this program and that manufacturing is conducted at the company's in-house commercial
facility.

About Krystal Biotech, Inc.
Krystal Biotech is a fully integrated, commercial-stage biotechnology company focused on the
development and commercialization of genetic medicines for patients with rare diseases.
